name: input.mouse.click
description: Synthesise a mouse click at a virtual-screen coordinate. Atomic press+release. Pass `duration_ms` to control the press-to-release gap (capped at 1000ms; longer holds use `input.mouse.press` + `input.mouse.release`).

double.description: If true, synthesises a double-click — two press/release pairs batched within `system.info.capabilities.input_settings.double_click_time_ms` so the OS double-click handler fires (used for word selection in text fields, double-click-to-open in shell views, etc.).

triple.description: If true, synthesises a triple-click — three press/release pairs batched within `system.info.capabilities.input_settings.double_click_time_ms` so the OS triple-click handler fires (used for line / paragraph selection in text fields). New in v2.2.

clicks.description: Issue N independent click events at this position, separated by `clicks_interval_ms`. Use this when you want N separate clicks the OS will NOT conflate into a double/triple-click event — e.g. test fixtures, rapid-fire inputs, scripted UI exercise. For OS-recognised multi-click events use `double` / `triple` instead. Range 2-10; values outside that window almost certainly indicate a caller bug. New in v2.2.

clicks_interval_ms.description: Inter-click gap in milliseconds for the `clicks` field. Only valid when `clicks` is set; rejected with `ERR invalid_args` otherwise. Default when omitted: `system.info.capabilities.input_settings.double_click_time_ms + 50` — explicitly outside the OS double-click window so the OS treats each click as an independent event. Set to 0 for back-to-back (which the OS may interpret as a double-click for clicks=2). New in v2.2.

duration_ms.description: Optional press-to-release gap in milliseconds (0-1000). Default = OS-minimum (a regular fast click). Useful for slow-press-detection workflows. Cap is 1 second; the verb is synchronous and longer holds belong on `input.mouse.press` + `input.mouse.release`. Mutually exclusive with `double`, `triple`, and `clicks` (a duration on a multi-click batch is ambiguous — use one or the other).

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held while clicking. Each modifier is synthesised down before the click and up after.

synthesised.description: True when the input event was accepted by user32's input queue. False indicates the agent detected a UIPI silent-drop (event accepted by the API but never delivered to a higher-IL target window). ERR uipi_blocked is still returned in the latter case; this field also reflects the same signal in the response body.

target_handle.description: Window handle that received the click, resolved via `WindowFromPoint(actual_position)` at synth time. Empty string when the click lands on the desktop or outside any window. Compare against the expected handle to detect target-moved races between window.list/find and the click.

x.description: Actual X the click landed at; differs from input when off-screen requests are clamped to the virtual-screen edge.

y.description: Actual Y the click landed at.

x-implementations.name: send_input
x-implementations.description: Win32 `SendInput` with INPUT_MOUSE structures. Modifier-down events bracket the click; double batches four mouse events in a single SendInput call, triple batches six, both within `GetDoubleClickTime` so the OS multi-click handler fires. `clicks: N` issues N separate SendInput calls (two events each) separated by `clicks_interval_ms` (default explicitly outside `GetDoubleClickTime` so each click stays independent). When `duration_ms > 0`, the agent issues the down event, sleeps via the request thread for the requested interval, then issues the up event — the connection is wedged for the duration.

x-implementations.name: mouse_event
x-implementations.description: Win32 `mouse_event` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x where `SendInput` is unavailable.

windows-modern.description: SendInput with INPUT_MOUSE structures. UIPI may silently drop synthesised input directed at higher-IL windows — agent post-checks (e.g. via WindowFromPoint comparison or GetLastInputInfo) and returns ERR uipi_blocked plus `synthesised: false`. When the event reaches user32 the field is true. `duration_ms` adds a Sleep between the down and up events; the call is synchronous so the connection blocks for that long. `triple` follows the same SendInput-batching path as `double` (six mouse events in one call instead of four). `clicks: N` issues N independent SendInput calls separated by `clicks_interval_ms`; the agent Sleeps between calls so the connection blocks for `(N-1) * clicks_interval_ms` total.

windows-classic.description: SendInput on NT 5+; mouse_event on NT 4 and 9x where SendInput is unavailable. No UIPI on classic, so synthesised input crosses process boundaries freely and `synthesised` is true on success. `duration_ms` behaves the same as on modern. `triple` and `clicks` follow the same batching pattern as on modern; on NT 4 / 9x `mouse_event` substitutes for SendInput but the inter-click timing model is identical.
